paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. Look at what Paul does with his time. He sends for the disciples and encourages them. He speaks "many words of encouragement" all through Macedonia (Acts 20:2). Then he gives the believers in Troas a whole night of the Word, because he's ready to leave the next day (Acts 20:7). The people of God gather around words, and Paul gives them everything he's got.

Now, Eutychus. I think this is the part that sticks. A young man sinks into a deep sleep, falls from the third story, and is "picked up dead" (Acts 20:9). Paul goes down, embraces him, and says, "Do not be alarmed!" and "He is still alive!" (Acts 20:10). I think the sleepy guy in the window is not the whole point here. God gives life in a moment that looked like the end. And the people were "greatly relieved to take the boy home alive" (Acts 20:12).

So what does that mean for you, baker? Show up and gather with God's people around the Word, even on the nights when you feel like that guy in the window. I've been in a dark drawer, so I know how a hopeless spot feels. God doesn't leave the story there. Paul goes back upstairs, breaks bread, and keeps speaking until daybreak (Acts 20:11). Keep your ovens ready, friend.
